title: First parades and the parks around New Orleans
summary: Marching at age six on alto, playing snare for Tony Sbarbaro, and locating Gretna, Algiers, McDonoghville dance parks.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Yeah, that's right. It must be. You didn't. Still, you must have worked on it. I mean you played so many jobs. Oh yeah. Tell me about, can you remember any, the first parade you played or any other parades?
Oh man, that's, I was six years old. How big were you?

I used to play snare drums sometimes with Tony Spago at the Dixieland Band and Biloxi in the Crockett Parade. He'd say, Bruno, take my drums, I'm tired. He's playing with, he's with the original New Orleans Dixieland Jazz Band. He plays the kazoo.
Yeah, still in New York I guess, yeah.
The first parades then you probably played alto horn.
Yeah, alto, and when the drummer didn't show up I had to switch the drums.

Oh, another question when you were speaking of Papa Lane, the Suburban Park. Papa Lane, we had an interview with him last year before our Ford Foundation grant went through. And he mentioned Suburban Park, was it? In McDonaville.

Or across the river. You see there's Gretna, there's McDonaville, and there's Algiers. Then up the upper part is Harvey's and West Wego and it's on the other side of the river. And the Crescent City Park is in Gretna, there's Bourbon Park, there's in McDonaville, and the Elvira Park is in Algiers. Then there was a club right on the river there by the ferry boat called the Owls Club, we used to play there a lot.
